flows.name: doc-audit-drift-interpretation-llm
flows.description: #362 (Moment 0 drift interpretation — narrow LLM judgment surface); cron-path invocation site corrected by #391. Per mapped drift event, the cron entry point `signals/drift_event.py::DriftEventSignalSource.commit()` delegates to the shared helper `routing/drift_moment0.py::route_drift_event()`, which invokes `drift_interpretation.interpret()` and routes the verdict. The library/CLI surface `helpers/handle_drift_events.py::process_events()` delegates to the same routing helper for operator replay (no longer the cron entry point). `interpret()` builds a cache-aware prompt and calls api.anthropic.com directly via the shared JudgmentClient (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). The verdict (PROPOSED_EDIT / JUDGMENT_REQUIRED / NO_CHANGE_NEEDED) plus confidence ∈ [0.0, 1.0] is parsed + validated against the E1 schema. PROPOSED_EDIT verdicts at confidence ≥0.80 feed drift_to_proposed_edit and onward through the existing tier_classification surface; lower confidence demotes to JUDGMENT_REQUIRED. Retry policy 30s/60s/120s; on exhaustion falls back to the pre-#362 issue path. Gated by [drift_interpretation].enabled in config.toml — flipping to false reverts to deterministic-only behavior in ≤60s (NFR-007).
flows.trigger: per drift event when [drift_interpretation].enabled = true in scripts/doc_audit/config.toml

flows.name: doc-audit-audit-interpretation-llm
flows.description: #400 (Moment 0 commit-audit interpretation — narrow per-doc LLM judgment surface mirroring drift_interpretation but adapted for commit-derived `Doc audit:` issues). When `handle_audit_routing.py` finds no deterministic-pattern proposals AND `[audit_interpretation].enabled = true`, the no-proposals branch invokes `audit_interpretation.interpret_audit(client, context)`. The helper assembles an AuditInterpretationContext (audit issue + commit SHA + diff + in-scope doc paths + per-doc current contents from disk) and calls api.anthropic.com once per in-scope doc via the shared JudgmentClient (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). Each call returns an AuditVerdict (PROPOSED_EDIT / JUDGMENT_REQUIRED / NO_CHANGE_NEEDED) with confidence ∈ [0.0, 1.0]. PROPOSED_EDIT at confidence ≥0.80 feeds the existing tier_classification surface (may yield Tier A auto-commit, Tier B pending-approval issue, or judgment debt-issue); PROPOSED_EDIT or NO_CHANGE_NEEDED at confidence <0.80 demotes to JUDGMENT_REQUIRED at the helper boundary. JUDGMENT_REQUIRED verdicts accumulate into a single consolidated comment posted to the audit issue (per research D3). When ALL in-scope docs return NO_CHANGE_NEEDED at confidence ≥0.80, the audit issue is auto-closed with a summary comment. Per-doc isolation: retry exhaustion on doc N does NOT prevent docs N±1 from being evaluated (synthetic JUDGMENT_REQUIRED verdict is emitted for the failed doc). Gated by [audit_interpretation].enabled in config.toml — flipping to false reverts to the pre-#400 no-proposals path (lock release + 'no automatable edits' comment) in ≤60s (FR-013).
flows.trigger: per commit-derived audit when handle_audit_routing.py finds no deterministic-pattern proposals AND [audit_interpretation].enabled = true in scripts/doc_audit/config.toml

path.description: No-proposals branch: assembles AuditInterpretationContext (audit_issue + commit_sha + diff + in_scope_doc_paths + per-doc current contents from disk) and calls interpret_audit(client, context). Returns list[AuditVerdict] (one per in-scope doc).
API key load via the shared JudgmentClient — not re-read per call; reused across the per-doc call sequence within a single audit. Sensitive: never logged.

ONE narrow judgment call PER in-scope doc. Per-doc retry exhaustion emits a synthetic JUDGMENT_REQUIRED verdict; catastrophic failures fall back to the pre-#400 lock-release + 'no automatable edits' comment path.

OpenClaw caches the system prompt for the lifetime of a session; AGENTS.md edits otherwise stay invisible until the next-started session. The cutover runbook (docs/runbooks/openclaw-agent-setup.md §'Cutover sequence for main-agent AGENTS.md changes (post-#374)') wraps this helper as step 4 of the 5-step deploy sequence. flows.name: signal-extraction-to-github
flows.description: #490 (signal-driven-monitoring-haiku-gate-01KT22PC) — deterministic OpenClaw log signal extraction files threshold-triggered issues to GitHub via kg-felix-bot. Each 15-min felix-core-digest tick chains summarize.py + tick.py (Type=oneshot, two ExecStart). tick.py reads /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-*.log, evaluates each configured signal (FR-001..FR-006), persists per-signal counters under /data/services/openclaw/felix-core-digest-signals/state/, and when a signal crosses its `cycle_threshold` / `rolling_threshold` AND no matching open issue exists within the dedup window, invokes scripts/openclaw/agents/main/felix-file-issue.py to file a new issue via gh under the kg-felix-bot identity. No LLM is in this path (NFR-003). Per-cycle outcomes land in last-tick.json + signals-ledger.jsonl. Log excerpts in issue bodies are credential-redacted per C-005. Replaces the prior heartbeat-driven LLM-judged filing path for the named signal classes; novel patterns continue to escalate via felix-heartbeat-gate (see heartbeat-gate-to-main-agent flow).
flows.trigger: every 15 minutes via felix-core-digest.timer (systemd user); also on manual `systemctl --user start --wait felix-core-digest.service`
flows.data_classification: operational telemetry (credential material redacted per C-005)

path.description: OnUnitActiveSec=15min, OnBootSec=3min, Persistent=true. Cadence unchanged from pre-#490.
Existing agent-log digest pass. Must exit 0 for tick.py to run (systemd Type=oneshot semantics).
Signal-extraction tick — only runs if summarize.py exited 0.
Reads the OpenClaw daily log(s) covering the rolling window per signal source. Read-only; no log mutation.

Persists per-signal counters (signal_id, count_in_window, last_event_at, last_filed_issue_ref, cycle_id) across ticks and restarts (FR-004). Cold-start logic re-reads recent log windows before trusting state.

On threshold cross with no matching open issue (FR-002). Invokes the existing template-compliant body builder so deterministic and LLM-authored filings are structurally indistinguishable (FR-003). On force_replay_filing=true path the helper enforces dry-run to prevent replay double-filing.

Per-cycle structured health signal: exit_status, started_at_utc, signals_evaluated, issues_filed, errors. Overwritten each cycle. Consumed by felix-heartbeat-gate as its primary input.

flows.name: heartbeat-gate-to-main-agent
flows.description: #490 (signal-driven-monitoring-haiku-gate-01KT22PC) — Haiku-tier routing gate decides whether each 30-minute heartbeat tick needs to wake the expensive Sonnet main-agent path. The gate (scripts/openclaw/heartbeat_gate/run.py) reads the latest signal-extraction snapshot (last-tick.json) and the heartbeat contract file (HEARTBEAT.md), assembles a cache-aware prompt, and calls claude-haiku-4-5 directly via the anthropic-python SDK. The gate returns one of HEARTBEAT_OK (do nothing), LOG_AND_SKIP (record but no action), or ESCALATE_TO_SONNET (wake the main agent with the gate's structured reason). On ESCALATE_TO_SONNET the gate invokes `openclaw system event --mode now` exactly once per tick (FR-008). On API error, timeout, or malformed-response the gate falls back to the same ESCALATE_TO_SONNET path so observation is never silently dropped (FR-011); the fallback is recorded in last-gate-decision.json.fallback_invoked. The gate honors the existing HEARTBEAT.md contract semantics (FR-010): scheduled tasks in the contract file are executed (cheap-tier where feasible, escalated when judgment is required). Replaces OpenClaw's internal heartbeat for the steady state; the internal heartbeat is disabled at cutover via `openclaw system heartbeat disable` (Tier 2 — see runbook).
flows.trigger: every 30 minutes via felix-heartbeat-gate.timer (systemd user); also on manual `systemctl --user start --wait felix-heartbeat-gate.service`
flows.data_classification: operational routing decision; gate prompt + response are logged in gate-ledger.jsonl (no credential material)

path.description: OnUnitActiveSec=30min, OnBootSec=5min, Persistent=true. 5-min boot offset avoids lockstep with felix-core-digest.timer (which uses OnBootSec=3min).
Direct Python invocation. Stateless per tick — no openclaw session, no carried-over LLM context.
Primary input — the signal-extraction snapshot from the last felix-core-digest tick. If missing or stale, the gate flags it in its context and biases toward ESCALATE_TO_SONNET.
Heartbeat contract file. Honored per the existing 'empty = skip' rule (FR-010). Scheduled tasks present here drive the routing decision.
Anthropic API key — same file as felix-doc-auditor-driver. Loaded once per tick into process memory; never logged or persisted in any output.

Single judgment call per tick to claude-haiku-4-5 with cache-aware prompt (stable system prompt + per-tick context). Returns strict-schema JSON; malformed responses trigger the fallback path (FR-011).

Invoked exactly once per tick on ESCALATE_TO_SONNET (FR-008). This wakes the existing OpenClaw main-agent (Sonnet 4.6) path with the gate's structured reason injected via the standard event-context mechanism. Also invoked on the fallback path (API failure, malformed response, timeout) so observation is never silently dropped (FR-011).
Existing expensive-tier path. Acts per existing conventions: files issues via felix-file-issue.py, sends WhatsApp messages, edits HEARTBEAT.md, etc.

Per-tick structured decision: outcome, reason, gate_latency_ms, gate_input_tokens, gate_cache_hit_tokens, gate_output_tokens, escalated_to, fallback_invoked, errors (FR-009). Overwritten each tick — canonical health-check surface.
Append-only ledger row per tick — backs cost telemetry (NFR-001) and post-rollout escalation review.

flows.name: inbox-calendar-create
flows.description: Flow A — Inbox-captured calendar event (one-off or recurring) auto-scheduled on Google Calendar with no Vikunja todo created. felix-admin-capture classifies the inbox note as a calendar event, validates required fields (title + start), and delegates the create payload to Felix main; main executes `gog calendar create` against the configured calendar. Default calendar is kent@intentional.biz primary; payload may override per-event.
flows.trigger: felix-admin-capture cron tick (inbox-7am/noon/5pm/10pm) classifies a note whose intent is a complete calendar event

path.description: Capture parses frontmatter + body, classifies intent, and validates calendar-event required fields (title, start)
Delegation payload includes the validated event fields (title, start, end/duration, attendees, location, recurrence, calendar override). Capture does not call gog directly.
Main is the gog process owner; executes `gog calendar create` with the delegated payload.

path.to: Google Calendar (kent@intentional.biz primary, or override per payload)
path.description: Auto-schedule the event without creating a Vikunja todo. Recurrence flows through gog's recurrence flags.

flows.purpose: Auto-schedule events submitted via inbox capture without creating Vikunja todos

flows.name: inbox-calendar-clarification-loop
flows.description: Flow B — Incomplete inbox-captured calendar event resolved through a single WhatsApp clarification round-trip. felix-admin-capture detects missing required fields, writes a deferred-event entry to the pending-calendar-clarifications state file (24h timeout sweep), and asks Kent one clarification question via WhatsApp. When Kent replies, Felix main reads the open clarification, merges the reply into the deferred payload, re-validates, and issues `gog calendar create`. Avoids losing the original capture context between the inbox tick and Kent's reply.
flows.trigger: felix-admin-capture classifies an inbox note as a calendar event but validation reports missing required fields

path.description: Capture detects missing required fields (e.g., missing start time, ambiguous duration)
Persists the deferred event payload + the open question for Kent. 24h timeout sweep cleans up stale entries.
Single clarification question sent to Kent. One question per cluster — never silently guesses.
Main receives the reply via the WhatsApp channel
Resolves Kent's reply against the open clarification entry; merges the reply into the deferred event payload.
Re-validates the merged payload and executes the deferred `gog calendar create` call.
Deferred event scheduled.

flows.purpose: Resolve incomplete calendar events through a single WhatsApp reply round-trip without losing context

flows.name: inbox-aspiration-to-journal
flows.description: Flow C — Inbox notes classified as aspirations or musings routed to the dated 08-Journal entry instead of becoming Vikunja todos. felix-admin-capture detects the aspiration/musing intent and appends the note body to `~/second-brain/notes/08-Journal/Journal YYYY-MM-DD HHmm.md`. No Vikunja todo is created; no delegation to gog or main. The dated journal is the canonical destination for non-actionable reflections.
flows.trigger: felix-admin-capture cron tick classifies an inbox note as an aspiration or musing (non-actionable reflection)

path.description: Capture classifies the note as aspiration/musing intent
Appends the note body to the dated journal entry. No Vikunja todo is created.

flows.purpose: Route aspirations and musings to the dated journal instead of Vikunja todos

flows.name: whatsapp-dm-reply
flows.description: Bidirectional DM-reply path. Inbound WhatsApp DM enters the openclaw-gateway; the gateway creates a session keyed `agent:main:whatsapp:direct:<peer>`; main agent processes the message (delegating to felix-admin-* subagents as appropriate); the agent's reply text reaches the channel-send subsystem; openclaw-gateway sends the reply back to the originating WhatsApp thread. Distinct from cron-driven announce-mode delivery (separate fire-and-forget path).

path.description: Operator sends a DM to Felix's WhatsApp number
Gateway creates a session, starts an embedded_run for the main agent; routes the inbound message as the agent's input
main agent classifies the DM intent and delegates to felix-admin-habits / felix-admin-tasker / felix-admin-escalation / felix-admin-calendar / felix-admin-capture per its AGENTS.md routing rules
Agent's reply text is returned through the embedded_run completion path; gateway invokes the WhatsApp plugin's send function
Reply delivered to the originating DM thread within seconds; typing indicator fires during the agent run

consumers.purpose: Top-level orchestrator; handles DM intent classification + delegation
Habit check-in queries via DM (delegation target)
Calendar event create + reply handling (delegation target)

flows.operational_notes: Per the embedded_run lifecycle contract (kitty-specs/restore-whatsapp-dm-reply-delivery-01KTVVHH/contracts/embedded-run-lifecycle.md): `embedded_run:started` must be followed by `embedded_run:ended` via `clearActiveEmbeddedRun`. If `clearActiveEmbeddedRun` is not called, the session enters the stuck-recovery path after ~378s, the run is aborted, and no reply is dispatched. See #588 + the openclaw-agent-setup runbook DM-reply troubleshooting section.

flows.description: The applier pulls from main on every tick, scans deploys/queued/ for new manifests, and applies them through lib.apply.dry_run_then_apply_gate. Replaces the historical Mac-push scp deploy path for office2-side services with a pull-based pipeline driven by a manifest queue on main.

path.description: Each tick performs `git pull origin main` against the repo mirror at /home/claude/kg-automation; transport is HTTPS via Tailscale exit node or public internet
Applier enumerates deploys/queued/<name>.yaml manifest files

flows.purpose: Provide a pull-based, manifest-driven deploy pipeline for office2-side services so deploys are committed to main, audit-trailed, and reversible — replacing the historical Mac-push scp pattern for kg-automation-managed surfaces.
